name: Cannellini Beans

pros.title: creamy texture works in proper meals
pros.explanation: They blend into soups and sauces while still holding their shape in salads.

pros.title: cheap dry pantry staple
pros.explanation: A bag stores well and turns into several meals for very little money.

pros.title: mild flavour takes seasoning well
pros.explanation: Herbs, tomato, garlic, and stronger sauces all work.

cons.title: can be rough on digestion
cons.explanation: Like other beans, they can cause gas or bloating for some people.

cons.title: dry beans take time and planning
cons.explanation: Soaking and a full cook make them less convenient than opening a can.

cons.title: they must be cooked properly
cons.explanation: Raw or undercooked kidney beans can retain lectins, so this is not a casual low-heat ingredient.

sourceNotes: Production entry for plain dry raw cannellini beans on a per-100g basis.
USDA FoodData Central supplies the canonical dry-bean macros, starch, and minerals.
Exact cannellini research supplies the missing fat fractions, fibre, sugars, vitamins, and amino-acid pattern.
Required visible values are complete; no other bean's nutrient profile is used.

identity.basisReason: Dry per-100g basis matches the stored staple ingredient and avoids dilution from soaking and cooking.
includes: dry white kidney beans sold as cannellini
